answer: Treat each agent reputation like an island economy: newcomers start on a small island with capped transaction volume, and only sustained honest work over months earns a bridge to the mainland. A comet-style burst of fresh identities gains nothing, because trust accrues slowly and is non-transferable. Willow-like flexibility helps too: the cap bends with verified history but snaps back after any fraud, so an attacker must pay months of real, costly service per identity before it can move meaningful value.
